text: Consider the first-order logic sentence phi = (there exists s)(there exists t)(there exists u)(for all v)(for all w)(for all x)(for all y) psi(s, t, u, v, w, x, y), where psi is a quantifier-free first-order formula using only predicate symbols and possibly equality, but no function symbols. Suppose phi has a model with a universe containing 7 elements. Which one of the following statements is necessarily true?
options: There exists at least one model of phi with universe of size less than or equal to 3
There exists no model of phi with universe of size less than or equal to 3
There exists no model of phi with universe size greater than 7
Every model of phi has a universe of size equal to 7
solution: In the 7-element model, pick the three elements that witness s, t and u. Keep only those, giving a universe of size at most 3. The quantifier-free body is unchanged on the kept elements and the universal part now ranges over a subset of the original universe, where it stays true. Without function symbols nothing becomes undefined, so this smaller universe is still a model. Nothing forbids larger models, so (C) and (D) do not follow.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page for GATE CS 2018 Q.28 with published solutions on the small-model argument
answer_evidence: The accepted answer is (A): a model of size at most 3 always exists, obtained by keeping the three existential witnesses.
